To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

opsonising antibody levels correlate with neutralizing antibody levels and that both uncomplexed virus as well as immune complexed virus stimulate plasmacytotic dendritic cells (DCs) via Toll-like receptor (TLR) 7.
1) FMDV opsonisation by non-neutralizing antibodies results in enhanced pDC activation and 2) the ability of FMDV to activate pDC varies between viral isolates.

the opsonizing antibody titers mediating enhanced interferon-alpha (IFN-α) responses in plasmacytold dendritic cells (DC) are similar to the neutralizing titers, when antigenically-related viruses from the same virus serotype are employed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of opsonising antibodies in FMDV clearance and the mechanisms involved.
the interplay between virus, antibody and pDC, which is a prerequisite for a better understanding of the mechanisms of protection against FMDV and the development of new vaccine strategies.
the role of antibody-mediated immune responses in the context of pDC and IFN-α production and the relevance of these findings for vaccine-induced immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the opsonisation of FMDV by antibodies is not a mechanism to be ignored in vaccine efficacy, but it is a mechanism that needs to be further investigated.
opsonising antibody responses may play an important role in antiviral responses, but the contribution may be different depending on the virus strain.

the opsonisation assay can be used to evaluate the presence of antibodies capable of enhancing IFN-α production by pDC and that the assay is useful to detect virus strains that are able to induce a strong pDC response, but it is not suitable as a general assay to evaluate the presence and/or titres of neutralizing antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
opsonisation of virus by antibodies can result in enhanced pDC responses, which in turn may contribute to the control of virus replication and the development of a protective immune response.
the interaction of FMDV, antibodies and pDC results in a fine tuned interplay, in which the virus is opsonized under non-neutralizing circumstances, resulting in enhanced IFN- α responses.
FMDV can be opsonized by non-neutralizing antibodies, which in turn can activate pDC via Toll-Like Receptor 7 to induce IFN-α.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pDC activation is not only mediated by virus-neutralizing antibodies and that pDC activation may contribute to the pathogenesis of FMDV infections.
pDC are a major player in FMDV infection and may contribute to the induction of IFN-α and the control of virus replication.
pDC activation via Toll-like receptor-7 can be enhanced by the opsonising capacity of antibodies and that this may be of importance in the immune response of animals to FMDV.
